subject: Georegulated tenant erase & evidence — process and timeline
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@aurorabio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraBio Security <security@aurorabio.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 07:22:00 +0000
Subject: Residency and tenant-directed erase for EU VPC deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. AuroraBio is preparing our compliance packet for an upcoming audit and we need to lock down the exact operational steps Redwood will take for a tenant-directed erase in our EU VPC deployment. Two direct asks from our security team:  

1) Can you provide an ordered list of actions Redwood will perform when AuroraBio requests a tenant erase (API call or support ticket)? Include expected timelines for each step (seconds/minutes/hours).
2) What artifacts will Redwood produce as proof of deletion (logs, checksums, storage-level wipe receipts)? We need something we can hand to auditors.

A couple of constraints: the VPC is customer-controlled S3-compatible object storage (we manage the bucket lifecycle) and Redwood has an encrypted cache tier in the private deployment. Please call out whether any data might transiently exist in cache or ephemeral compute and how that is handled.

If you can share a short summary + an evidence checklist, that would be ideal — we can follow up with SOC if needed.

Appreciate the help,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of InfoSec Programs, AuroraBio
security@aurorabio.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency and tenant-directed erase for EU VPC deployment

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear asks. I captured these into two parts below: a short operational summary you can include in the packet, and a checklist of evidence items. I don’t want to overpromise on anything sensitive, so I’ve looped in Rishi (security) and Monica (CS) to confirm we can provide the artifacts and timelines you need.

Operational summary (high level)
- Trigger: AuroraBio issues a tenant-erase via the Redwood Console or a signed support ticket API request.
- Immediate: Redwood validates request ownership and captures a request-id (seconds).
- Phase 1 (storage unlink): Redwood revokes access keys to the tenant slice and removes DNS/route entries (1–5 min). For customer-managed buckets we mark the tenant as "deleted" in our catalog and issue the erase checklist; object deletion is initiated from AuroraBio side or via your lifecycle policy — Redwood will remove any references and cached copies.
- Phase 2 (cache + runtime): Our runtime flushes KV/prefix caches, clears in-memory KV shards, and orchestrates a secure zeroing of ephemeral GPU scratch if present (minutes depending on queue).
- Phase 3 (index and metadata): We delete tenant metadata, search indices, and KV pointers from our control plane (minutes).
- Finalization: System emits a deletion-complete event and generates an evidence package (audit logs + manifests) (minutes to an hour depending on backlog).

Evidence checklist (what we can provide)
- Deletion request record (request-id, initiator, timestamp).
- Access revocation log (when keys/routes were removed).
- Control plane delete audit trail with object references (manifest).
- Cache flush receipts (service logs showing cache purge for tenant id).
- Ephemeral instance termination events and zeroization markers (where supported).
- SHA256 manifest of deleted metadata and a signed timestamp.

Notes / constraints
- For customer-managed object storage (your S3 bucket) Redwood does not physically delete objects inside a bucket we do not control; we will remove our references and, if requested, can coordinate with your infra team to run lifecycle deletion or provide guidance for object-level erase.
- Ephemeral compute: on-prem/private runtime supports secure-erase routines for GPU scratch where hardware permits; timing varies.
- We can produce a signed PDF summary and CSV manifest for auditors.

I’ll hold sending the formal evidence package until Rishi confirms the specific artifact formats. Monica — can you confirm if CS needs a courtesy note to AuroraBio when we start the erase?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks for the clear summary, Kimberly. Confirming what we can commit to and the expected timelines (I’ve kept best-case vs typical below). I attached a short runbook and a residency evidence spreadsheet.

What Security can sign / provide
- Signed deletion-complete statement (PDF) containing request-id, tenant id, timestamps, and signed SHA256 manifest (Best-case: within 1 hour of finalization; Typical: 1–6 hours depending on queue).
- Control-plane audit log extract (JSON/CSV) showing all delete operations for the tenant (Typical: 30–90 minutes to prepare sanitized extract).
- Cache purge logs (service logs showing purge calls and timestamps). Some of these are internal service entries; we will include redacted traces suitable for auditors.
- Hardware zeroization marker: where the private deployment hardware supports secure-erase we will include the termination events and a zeroization marker. (Best-case: minutes; Typical: up to 2 hours if instances need draining.)

Constraints and coordination notes
- Customer-managed object storage: Redwood cannot physically remove objects inside a bucket you own. We will provide a manifest of object keys we referenced and the timestamps of when those references were dropped. For auditors, AuroraBio should run the bucket-level lifecycle or object deletion policy after our reference removal, or grant a one-time lifecycle override.
- Ephemeral cache: transient in-memory or KV caches are flushed on command. We provide cache flush receipts; however, we cannot produce physical media-level overwrite proof for RAM — the evidence is operational (logs + event markers).

Next steps
1) AuroraBio to confirm preferred artifact format (signed PDF + CSV manifest) and a preferred window for the operation.
2) Monica / CS to coordinate a maintenance window if AuroraBio wants a low-latency completion (queue/backlog can extend timelines).
3) Redwood Security will prepare the evidence package and deliver via the secure artifact link (we use signed Drive/Confluence links).

Attachments: data_erase_runbook.pdf (internal runbook, redacted for public sharing), residency_evidence_summary.xlsx (manifest template).

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security — Redwood Inference
